issues.legal_issue: A mortgagor may deposit the amount required to redeem the mortgage while an appeal concerning the refusal to restore an application to set aside the execution sale remains pending, even if the sale has been confirmed in the meantime.
material_facts: The property had been sold in execution of a mortgage decree, and the mortgagor’s application to set aside the sale was dismissed for default before the sale was confirmed.

The mortgagor sought restoration of that application and challenged the refusal to restore it and the refusal to set aside confirmation; those challenges were pending when the mortgagor applied to deposit the balance of the mortgage money.
The High Court directed that the deposit be accepted without prejudice to the parties’ contentions, and the executing court accepted the deposit and recorded that the mortgage was discharged.
The executing court’s acceptance of the deposit was not challenged by the mortgagee, and the High Court subsequently ordered the mortgage documents returned.
issues.conclusion: The deposit application was maintainable while the appeals concerning the sale objections were pending. The confirmation of sale was not final during that period, so the mortgagor could redeem the mortgage by making the required deposit; the mortgage was discharged and the documents were returnable.
issues.legal_principle: Order 34 Rule 5 CPC allows a mortgagor to pay the amounts due before confirmation of sale, with the additional deposit required when the property has been sold; Rule 5A concerns return of documents. Under Order 21 Rule 92, confirmation follows when no application to set aside the sale is made or such an application is disallowed, but confirmation does not attain finality while an appeal concerning the validity of the sale is pending. That remains so when the appeal challenges refusal to restore an application dismissed for default, because restoration can return the parties to the position in which the sale objection is pending. The Court relied on Chandra Mani Saha v. Anarjan Bibi, Maganlal v. Jaiswal Industries, Varadarajan v. Venkatapathy Reddy, Ramathal v. Nagarathinammal and Satyanarayana v. Ramamurthi, and distinguished Hukamchand v. Bansilal, which addressed the court repeatedly postponing confirmation to accommodate a judgment-debtor.

predicates.mortgage_decree_execution: The proceeding concerns execution of a decree for sale of property mortgaged to secure a debt.
predicates.sale_set_aside_application_dismissed_for: The mortgagor’s application to set aside the execution sale was dismissed because the mortgagor did not pursue it.
predicates.restoration_or_sale_validity_appeal_pend: An appeal is pending concerning refusal to restore the sale objection or otherwise concerning the validity of the execution sale.
predicates.redemption_deposit_made_before_appeal_di: The mortgagor applies to deposit the redemption amount before the pending appeal is disposed of.

issues.definition: When a mortgage sale is under challenge in a pending appeal after the sale objection was dismissed for default, a redemption deposit made before that appeal ends permits redemption before the sale becomes final.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may use its power to grant consequential relief in related appeals to reconcile inconsistent orders, even when the party benefiting from that relief did not separately appeal.
material_facts: The High Court dismissed appeals concerning the dismissal of the mortgagor’s restoration and sale-objection applications but allowed a related revision concerning return of the mortgage documents.

In allowing the revision, the High Court held that the accepted redemption deposit had discharged the mortgage and that the documents should be returned, creating an inconsistency with its dismissal of the related appeals.
The mortgagor had not appealed to the Supreme Court against the dismissal of those appeals, but the Supreme Court allowed them to bring the related rulings into harmony.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court invoked Order 41 Rule 33 CPC to allow the related appeals and remove the inconsistency, notwithstanding the absence of a separate appeal by the mortgagor against their dismissal.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rule 33 CPC permits an appellate court to make the order that ought to have been made and to grant consequential relief necessary to do complete justice between the parties. The Court relied on that provision to reconcile the related appellate outcomes; no earlier case was cited for this particular application of the provision.

predicates.related_appellate_proceedings: More than one appeal or related appellate proceeding concerns connected orders in the same dispute.
predicates.related_orders_inconsistent: The outcomes in the related proceedings cannot be reconciled with one another.
predicates.consequential_relief_needed_for_consiste: Granting consequential relief is needed to make the related outcomes consistent and to do justice between the parties.
predicates.benefiting_party_did_not_separately_appe: The party who would benefit from the consequential relief did not separately appeal the adverse order.

issues.definition: When related appellate outcomes conflict and consequential relief is needed to reconcile them, the appellate court may grant that relief even if its beneficiary did not separately appeal.
